items.title: Jimmy and Jeannie Cheatham interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions watching 'High Society' with Bing Crosby and Louis Armstrong; Interviewee does not mention any personal interaction with Bing Crosby.

ctx.x: Because jazz has to be listened to, and if they can hear it from people who have done it, instead of imagining what’s going down, they can at least see us. © Fillius Jazz Archive -37-

And the most important thing, if they can see and hear it simultaneously. So if it’s live it’s even greater, but if not, hey, a videotape or a movie, old movies and things like that, if it’s no more than that one little slot. Where like “High Society” we were talking about coming here, and I was watching it the other night, on the late T.V. movie, with Bing Crosby and Louis Armstrong, and Frank Sinatra. And it was a beautiful thing to see. Louis opened up the whole picture you know, and he said now the story…
No one else could have pulled that off.
